topic: Stock Exchanges, SEBI, and Indices of Economics
description: The capital market is a vital part of the financial system where long-term securities are traded. In India, trading primarily occurs through major stock exchanges, with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) acting as the apex regulatory authority to protect investors and ensure market integrity.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of the Stock Market
sections.description: Fundamental technical terms and definitions related to the stock and capital markets.

key_concepts.explanation: The process by which a privately held, unlisted company issues its shares to the general public for the first time to raise capital.
An account used by investors to hold shares and other securities in an electronic (dematerialized) format rather than as physical certificates.
A 'Bull' is an optimistic investor who expects stock prices to rise and buys shares, while a 'Bear' is a pessimistic investor who expects prices to fall and sells shares.
Large, well-established, and financially sound companies with a stellar reputation, reliable performance, and a history of consistent dividend payments.

sections.title: Major Stock Exchanges of India
sections.description: Historical development and key facts about India's two largest stock exchanges: BSE and NSE.

historical_events.event: Establishment of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE)
historical_events.significance: Founded by Premchand Roychand under a banyan tree. It is the oldest stock exchange not only in India but in all of Asia.

historical_events.event: Establishment of the National Stock Exchange (NSE)
historical_events.significance: Established on the recommendation of the Pherwani Committee, it became the first fully automated screen-based electronic trading platform in India.

important_facts.fact: The original name of the BSE was 'The Native Share & Stock Brokers Association'.
By trading volume and market capitalization, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) is currently the largest stock exchange in India.

sections.title: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
sections.description: The history and role of SEBI as the apex regulatory body of the Indian capital and securities market.

historical_events.significance: Initially established as a non-statutory body through an executive resolution of the Government of India.
Granted autonomous and statutory status through the passing of the SEBI Act, 1992 by the Indian Parliament.

key_concepts.explanation: The illegal practice of trading on the stock exchange to one's own advantage by having access to confidential, non-public information. SEBI actively monitors and prevents this to protect regular investors.

important_facts.fact: SEBI's headquarters are located in Mumbai, with regional offices in New Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, and Ahmedabad.
Madhabi Puri Buch is the first woman to be appointed as the Chairperson of SEBI.

sections.title: Major Global and Indian Indices
sections.description: Key stock market indices that measure and represent the performance of various stock exchanges globally and in India.

key_associations.extra_info: Represents the performance of the top 30 well-established companies listed on the BSE. Its base year is 1978-79.
Represents the weighted average of the top 50 largest Indian companies listed on the NSE.
NASDAQ is globally notable for being heavily weighted towards major information technology companies.
The leading and most widely respected index of Japanese stocks.
The representative stock market index of the Korea Exchange.
A highly followed, free-float-adjusted market-capitalization-weighted stock market index in Asia.

sections.title: Instruments of the Capital Market
sections.description: Various financial instruments used by corporations and governments to raise funds from the market.

key_concepts.explanation: Represents real fractional ownership in a company, granting the shareholders voting rights and a claim on corporate dividends.
Long-term debt instruments issued by companies to borrow money at a fixed interest rate, without giving up any ownership or voting rights.
A professionally managed investment trust that pools money from many retail investors to purchase a diversified portfolio of securities like stocks and bonds.
The market for government and semi-government securities. These are considered highly secure and risk-free because there is practically no risk of default.
